extracted.intended_audience: startup founders, PR/communications teams, and product/marketing managers writing partnership announcement press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and an evaluative checklist for producing partnership announcement press releases that merit publicity and clearly communicate customer impact, timing, and strategic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material to revenue or product
rubrics_metrics.description: The partnership must be material to the company's revenue or product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include evidence of materiality (e.g., revenue impact, product integration that changes offering). If the partnership is marginal to core business, it's not newsworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer impact significant
rubrics_metrics.description: The partnership produces significant impact for customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific customer benefits, measurable outcomes, named customers or use cases; avoid vague claims. Significant impact can be time/cost savings, new capabilities, or measurable performance gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic positioning shift
rubrics_metrics.description: The partnership signals a strategic shift or repositions the company in the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the partnership changes market positioning or strategy, not just routine cooperation. Tie to market context or competitive dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Named, recognizable partner
rubrics_metrics.description: The partner is a named, recognizable company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcements are stronger when the partner is well-known or lends credibility. For lesser-known partners, emphasize the specific capability or customer relevance they bring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive arrangement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement is exclusive (or meaningfully differentiated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusive deals increase newsworthiness. If non-exclusive, show why this arrangement is distinct (e.g., deeper integration, co-development).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard customer relationship (not newsworthy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine customer relationships generally do not warrant a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid announcing ordinary vendor-customer deals unless there is an unusual scope, scale, or strategic value. Use customer case studies or joint marketing only if impact is substantial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reseller arrangement (not newsworthy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple reseller agreements typically do not merit a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reseller relationships are often transactional; only announce if the arrangement materially changes distribution reach or product availability in a meaningful way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliate program (not newsworthy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affiliate program relationships are not normally press-worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal marketing or partner program updates belong in partner communications rather than public press releases unless tied to significant new reach or revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 'integration' (not newsworthy)
rubrics_metrics.description: A vague or generic integration announcement is unlikely to be newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If announcing an integration, specify what joint capability is enabled and the tangible customer benefit—avoid one-line 'we integrated with X' releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exclusive arrangement with minor party (not newsworthy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-exclusive deals with minor parties usually don't justify a press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the partner is small or the deal is non-exclusive, focus on outcomes or customer impact if you must announce; otherwise coordinate smaller partner communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid calling it a 'strategic partnership' without strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't label an arrangement a 'strategic partnership' if you don't describe the strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete strategic rationale and specifics rather than relying on buzzwords. Review copy for empty labels and require an explanation of strategic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'combining forces' buzzword language
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid platitudes like 'combining forces' that say nothing substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precise language about capabilities, roles, and outcomes. Replace buzzwords with concrete descriptions of what is changing and why it matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid partner quotes that are purely promotional
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes from partners should not be just promotional fluff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require quotes that add strategic insight or specifics about what the partnership enables; remove or rewrite quotes that merely market without substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: State specific outcomes for customers
rubrics_metrics.description: The release must state specific outcomes customers will see.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List measurable benefits or capabilities enabled by the partnership (e.g., 'reduces processing time by X', 'adds Y functionality'). Avoid vague benefit statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a timeline for joint work
rubrics_metrics.description: Include when the joint capability or offering will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give exact dates or clear availability windows. Absence of timing undermines credibility and can be perceived as premature PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: '[Company A] and [Company B] Partner to [Specific Joint Outcome]'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a headline that names both companies and a specific joint outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headline focused and outcome-oriented. Avoid generic headlines; make the customer-facing result clear in the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: clear announcement with specific outcome, customer benefit, and start date
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph should state the partnership, specific outcome, customer benefit, and when it starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the template: '[Company A] and [Company B] today announced a partnership to [specific outcome]. The collaboration will [specific customer benefit] starting [specific date].' Keep it succinct and factual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: Specific joint capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the specific joint capability enabled by the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what the partnership makes possible in concrete terms rather than high-level claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: What customers can do that they couldn't before
rubrics_metrics.description: State what new actions or outcomes customers can achieve post-partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast previous limitations with new capabilities; use concrete examples or task-based descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: Timeline of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the timeline for when the capability or offering will be available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give specific dates or phased availability details and any geographic rollouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: Geographic scope if relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate geographic scope of availability (regions, countries, markets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about where the offering will be available and note any market limitations or rollouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2: Market context driving the partnership
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the market context or customer problems motivating the partnership now.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie the partnership to trends, competitive pressures, or customer pain points that justify the collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2: Each company's contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Detail what each company brings to the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify roles, technologies, distribution, or expertise each party contributes; avoid vague attributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2: Why these two specifically
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why these two companies are partnering rather than other potential partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight complementary assets, prior work together, or unique alignment that makes the partnership logical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: Named customer if possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a named customer or partner reference when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A customer reference adds credibility—obtain permission and present a concise case study or quote when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: Specific use case
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concrete use case illustrating how customers will use the joint capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a short, real-world example that demonstrates value and context for typical customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: Measurable benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: State a measurable benefit (metrics, KPIs) customers can expect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer quantifiable claims (e.g., percentage improvement, time saved). If precise numbers are unavailable, give clear directional benefits and how they'll be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: Migration path if existing customers
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how existing customers migrate or adopt the new capability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear steps, timelines, or support options for current customers to transition or enable the joint offering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 4: CEO from each company quoted
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a quote from each company's CEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEO quotes should add strategic perspective and not merely repeat the product copy; if CEOs aren't appropriate, use senior executives who can speak to strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 4: Quotes substantive on strategic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes should articulate strategic value, not promotional fluff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure quotes explain why the partnership matters strategically and how it benefits customers; edit partner quotes to remove empty marketing language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 4: Quotes specific on what's enabled
rubrics_metrics.description: Quotes should be specific about what the partnership enables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage detail in quotes (e.g., features, workflows, customer outcomes) rather than generic praise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: both companies' descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Include standard boilerplate describing each company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boilerplates should be concise, factual, and include primary positioning for each company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: combined scale or reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention combined scale or reach where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the partnership increases scale (users, customers, markets), quantify or describe that reach in the boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate: headquarters and founded dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include headquarters and founding dates in boilerplates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic factual details like HQ and founding year help media and readers contextualize the companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same day release from both companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate to release the announcement the same day from both companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synchronize embargoes and publication timing; ensure both PR teams share the final copy and timing plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with sales teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate the announcement with sales teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform and align sales teams on messaging, FAQ, and any sales enablement materials prior to the public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customer notification first
rubrics_metrics.description: Notify customers before the public announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide customers with context and migration options before the news goes public to avoid surprises and confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire from both wires (PRN + BW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute the release on wire services from both companies (e.g., PRN and Business Wire).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual wire distribution increases reach and signals joint commitment; ensure consistent messaging across wires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-promotional social
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate co-promotional social media posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan synchronized social posts, approved messaging, and hashtags; leverage both companies' channels for amplification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint webinar or event
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan a joint webinar or event to promote the partnership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use joint events to demonstrate the integration, provide demos, and answer customer questions—coordinate timing and registrant outreach.
